phase_7_ce_018_new_cemetery_theorem.what_was_proposed: Reusable rule: before any novelty claim, the candidate must survive a CAPABILITY collision test against the prior art landscape. The test asks: 'Could a skilled person reconstruct the proposed element from the entire relevant technological neighborhood?' — NOT 'Did anyone use our exact phrase?' The test maps the candidate's capabilities (what it can DO) to prior art capabilities, and requires that at least one capability be genuinely unoccupied (not just reworded).
phase_7_ce_018_new_cemetery_theorem.why_it_failed: Originated from the Round 60/61 → Round 62 sequence. Round 60/61 searched 6 CE-014 vectors using the candidate's own vocabulary ('retrieved-clot physical signature') and found zero blocking prior art. Round 62 CEO audit found 3 direct prior art collisions (US20250186070A1, US20230062684A1, EP3763305A1 — though 2 of 3 appear to be mis-citations) plus Clotild/Sensome commercial frontier, all occupying the broad capability landscape. The Round 60/61 search PASSED on keyword collision but FAILED on capability collision.
phase_7_ce_018_new_cemetery_theorem.reusable_lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT search for your candidate's exact phrase — search for the capability it provides
Do NOT use semantic distinctions ('retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ') as novelty loopholes — this is CE-012 violation
Do NOT conclude novelty from keyword-collision search alone — capability collision is mandatory
Do NOT ignore commercial frontier evidence (Clotild/Sensome) — it occupies capabilities even without a patent
Do NOT assume your search vocabulary matches the prior art's vocabulary — use CE-014 multi-vector multi-vocabulary search on the CAPABILITY, not the candidate
phase_7_ce_018_new_cemetery_theorem.physical_constraint: BOUNDED. The capability collision test is operationally harder than keyword collision test because it requires decomposing the candidate into functional capabilities and searching each against the prior art landscape using the prior art's own vocabulary. But it is the only test that catches the CE-012 failure mode (semantic re-skin of known capability).
